candidates.creator: Anthropic42
candidates.title: Beach sounds South Carolina.ogg
candidates.sourceFormat: Ogg Vorbis; Commons reports 1 min 2 s / 137 kbps; inspect exact stream after acquisition
use: possible CoastalWind bed only if human listening proves useful wind character
candidates.provenance: Natural recording made at Litchfield Beach near Pawleys Island, South Carolina on 25 December 2003 using Sony MiniDisc and an AudioTechnica stereo microphone; released into the public domain by its author.
candidates.caveat: Metadata proves a real beach recording and strong recording provenance, not that the wind component is dominant or suitable for SFX_AMB_Beach_CoastalWind. Human listening must separate surf/water character from usable coastal wind before any coverage/derivation decision.

candidates.creator: syncopika
candidates.title: cricket sounds — cricketsounds090613.wav
candidates.provenance: Uploader states this was captured fresh in their backyard and recorded directly to Audacity via the built-in microphone of a Toshiba NB505 netbook.
candidates.caveat: Uploader explicitly says recording quality is not great. Human listening must reject laptop-mic noise, unsuitable biome character or insufficient clean variation; filename semantics do not imply approval.

candidates.provenance: Wikimedia Commons states thunder was recorded in Southern Finland on Minidisc by uploader Mysid; copyright holder released the work into the public domain worldwide.
candidates.caveat: Metadata proves natural thunder and provenance, not perceived distance. Do not mark SFX_WTH_Thunder_Near covered until human listening confirms suitable near-event character, transient and tail.

candidates.creator: avphillips
candidates.title: Gull 1
candidates.sourceFormat: Ogg Vorbis; Commons reports 18 s / 74 kbps; historical PDSounds source was mono 22 kHz-class material
candidates.provenance: PDSounds recording by avphillips, tagged Bird/Gull/Shore and documented as Herring Gull on Long Island, USA, September 1999; author released the recording into the public domain and Commons preserves the transfer/provenance chain.
candidates.caveat: Commons file is a transcoded derivative of the older public-domain PDSounds source. Preserve acquired bytes and avoid repeated lossy transcodes; human listening must reject codec/ambient artifacts and verify island-context fit.

candidates.creator: Escoitar.org
candidates.title: Vento fisterra.ogg

candidates.creator: ezwa
candidates.title: Walk in the rainforest
candidates.sourceFormat: Ogg Vorbis; Commons reports 31 s / 121 kbps; historical PDSounds source was MP3 mono 44 kHz 128 kbps
use: possible low-detail bed or supporting fauna layer if human listening supports it
candidates.provenance: PDSounds recording by ezwa, described as sounds on a walk in the Guadeloupean rainforest; natural recording transferred to Wikimedia Commons and released into the public domain by its author.
candidates.caveat: Metadata explicitly tags birds/birdsong and the recording was made while walking. Do not promote it as a stable deep bed if footsteps, handling noise or dominant close birds make the perspective too active; it is not a canopy-wind source.

rejectedDuringResearch.reason: OGA page is CC0-labelled, but uploader states the recordings originated in a third-party video shared with permission. Provenance chain is weaker than project policy requires for a new canonical source candidate.
CC0 page, but thunder is described as built from plugins/mixed production rather than a clean natural thunder field source. Not suitable for the natural near-thunder source role.
Natural CC0 storm recording but deliberately contains repeated flood siren events, making it unsuitable as clean storm/thunder source material for the island context.
Natural thunder source but licensed CC BY 3.0/GFDL; the current preferred field-source lane accepts CC0 or Public Domain when an equally useful candidate is available.

Public-domain forest recording, but uploader documents substantial microphone noise and dominant crow interruptions; not promoted as a clean jungle/deep-bed source merely because tags mention jungle/nature.
CC0 own-work wind recording, but the source is wind howling in a building; the enclosed space identity is wrong for an open-island storm/coastal role.
Useful visual/ocean material but supplied as large Ogg Theora video containers rather than clean audio originals; not used as audio-source masters when better field-audio hygiene is required.

rule: A field-backlog candidate remains candidate-only until the acquisition workflow has captured exact bytes, technical metadata and SHA-256; human listening is still required before any source approval.
